title: Paffett wins the Hockenheim opener from pole as Mercedes fills the top two
dek: Gary Paffett won DTM Race 1 at Hockenheim from pole, 1.449 seconds ahead of team-mate Lucas Auer, after an early pit stop turned the lead round; BMW’s Timo Glock was third.

chapters.title: A new rulebook and a farewell season
text: The DTM opened its 2018 season at Hockenheim on 4–6 May with two big questions hanging over it. This was Mercedes-AMG’s final year in the championship, and the cars had been reshaped over the winter: more standard parts and simpler wings cut downforce by roughly 30 per cent, the minimum weight fell to 1,115kg, and each manufacturer could use eight engines over the season instead of seven. The aim was to put more emphasis on braking and the driver, and to make the cars easier to follow.

Audi arrived as the team to beat. It had won all three titles in 2017, and René Rast was the defending champion, in a line-up where Robin Frijns replaced Mattias Ekström. Ekström was back for one last weekend all the same, in a seventh RS 5 running as a guest outside the points. Mercedes had Pascal Wehrlein and Daniel Juncadella back in place of Maro Engel and Robert Wickens, while BMW, led by two-time champion Marco Wittmann, fielded two rookies in Joel Eriksson and Philipp Eng. Each race would last 55 minutes plus one lap, and the top three in qualifying were to earn three, two and one championship points.

chapters.title: Paffett’s first-run lap holds, Audi is left behind
text: Gary Paffett took the first pole of the new era with a 1m32.264s, set on the first runs, and he could not improve on his second set. The time was more than a second and a half slower than the previous year’s pole, a direct result of the cut in downforce. Marco Wittmann found three personal-best sectors late in the session to climb to second, 0.199 seconds behind, and Timo Glock was third, 0.204 off, after complaining that his tyre pressures rose too quickly on the second set and left him without front-end grip from Turn 6.

Lucas Auer was fourth, a further 0.016 seconds back, and Pascal Wehrlein, on his DTM comeback, was fifth just two thousandths behind the Austrian. Augusto Farfus, Edoardo Mortara and Bruno Spengler followed, so the top ten held four Mercedes and five BMWs, with Rast the only Audi among them.

Audi had a much harder time. Rast was the best of them in ninth, 0.516 seconds off the pole, and the four slowest cars on the grid were all Audis: Loïc Duval 16th, having also been racing at Spa that weekend, then Frijns, Ekström and Jamie Green, 0.986 seconds off the time of the leader and last on the grid. Audi motorsport chief Dieter Gass put the deficit at about half a second and said it was hard to make that up in a race.

chapters.title: Auer drives through to the lead
text: Paffett made a good start and led into the first corner, with Wittmann second. The field got through the first lap without contact, but Eng, in his first DTM race, almost stood still when the lights went out and dropped to the back of the field.

The race began to move on lap one. Auer, who started fourth, passed Glock at the end of the opening lap, took Wittmann at the hairpin on the second and then closed on his team-mate. On lap four he went past Paffett for the lead at the hairpin, while Glock also passed Wittmann for third and Wehrlein came up behind the two BMWs. Paffett said he did not want to fight Auer too hard and chose to bring his stop forward instead.

chapters.title: Paffett’s undercut turns the race
text: The stops started with Glock and Wittmann around the end of lap 11. That forced Paffett to come in earlier than he had planned, and he stopped a lap before Auer, with a strong stop and a fast out-lap on tyres that were already up to temperature. Auer’s in-lap was poor and his stop slower, and although he rejoined narrowly ahead of Paffett, he was on colder tyres with less grip and the Briton was through again at the hairpin.

Glock, just behind, then turned on Auer. He attacked for second several times, going side by side with the Mercedes, but the Austrian covered the inside and held the place. Glock said afterwards that his tyres would only last two laps behind another car, and that Auer had defended cleverly.

Further back the stops brought drama of a different kind. Rast and Juncadella pitted together, and Rast’s crew released him as the Mercedes was passing, which left the two cars side by side in the pit lane. The incident was sent to the stewards for review after the race. Mortara ran a long first stint, which gave him fresher tyres for the second half.

chapters.title: Paffett cruises home as Mercedes takes the points
text: In the second stint Paffett’s car was, in his words, incredible. He built a lead of almost three seconds, then eased off and let Auer close it to 1.449 seconds at the flag for his first DTM victory since 2013 and the 21st of his career. Glock, who had spent the stint bothering Auer, took the last podium place 6.514 seconds behind the winner.

Mortara’s long first stint paid off. On fresh tyres he picked off places and went past Wehrlein for fourth, having started seventh, with Wehrlein fifth in his first race since leaving Formula 1. Spengler was sixth, the best BMW after Glock, and Paul di Resta and Juncadella, who set the fastest lap of the race, took seventh and eighth after starting 12th and 13th. All six Mercedes finished in the top ten.

It was a bad afternoon for the others. Wittmann, who had started on the front row, dropped to 11th as his tyres wore, and Audi’s only points went to Rast in ninth and Duval in tenth. Gass said the rule changes had cost Audi more than its rivals, and that nobody should expect to turn the result upside down on Sunday. Mercedes team boss Ulrich Fritz, meanwhile, called it a start that could hardly have gone better, with a one-two, fourth and fifth, and seventh and eighth.

facts.v: Paffett’s Hockenheim victory was his first in the DTM since the Lausitzring in 2013 and the 21st of his career.
